content.thinking:
Skipping the kit for this low-poly build, I'm planning the elephant's proportions instead: shoulder height around 3.2m, body length 3.6m, tusks 1.5-2m, with a skeleton rooted at the hips in a model facing +Z.

Body barrel spans rump to chest with a dipped back typical of African elephants, belly clearance around 1m, head and ears oversized relative to body with trunk reaching the ground. I'm working out the spine chain from hips through shoulders to neck and head, plus a separate tail chain extending backward from the hips root joint.

I'll root the spine chain at the hips joint position, with the tail as a separate chain also parented there, starting near the rump. Then I'm working out the body loft stations—z positions with center height, width, and height values—to shape the rump tapering into the torso.

Continuing through the loft: torso stays wide through the chest, narrows toward the neck/shoulder front, and I'm adjusting the back profile so it dips slightly in the middle like an African elephant, with a shoulder withers bump around z=0.9 to get the right top height near 3.15-3.2.

For legs, I'm treating them as pillar-like columns with slight bend, mapping shoulder-to-elbow-to-knee-to-foot joint positions and segment lengths so the front limb chain spans roughly 1.78-1.9 units with a mild bend at the knee rather than being perfectly straight.

I'm settling on radii around [0.34, 0.27, 0.25] for the leg taper, aiming for a realistic ~0.45m front leg diameter. For the foot, I'm figuring out how the sweep's end cap should sit so the tube's rounded bottom lands flush with the floor rather than poking below it, adjusting the final joint height accordingly.

Now I'm planning the feet in detail: flat end caps with an 8-sided faceted cross-section, landing just above the floor for tolerance, plus toenail blocks (4-5 on front feet, 3-4 on hind) and a wrinkled-skin cuff ring near the ankle. For the hind legs, I'm placing the hip and foot target points and thinking through how the knee bends forward while the hock bends back, working out appropriate segment lengths for the elephant's proportions.

Checking the hind leg segments—femur, tibia, foot with lengths 0.85/0.7/0.4 and alternating bend directions—the total length slightly exceeds the straight-line distance, giving a natural mild bend. I'm also noting that the hips sit high enough that the upper legs partially bury into the body volume, which is fine given the leg's thick upper radius, and that legs should parent to the spine (front) or hips (hind) joints. Now I'm moving on to the head, planning a domed elephant skull lofted from a joint positioned above and in front of the shoulders.

Working out the cranium loft stations—sizing width and height at each z-position from the brow down toward where the trunk emerges—to get that bulging forehead and tapering face, with the head top sitting around shoulder height. I'm placing the head joint and then figuring out where to sprout the trunk from the front of the face, hanging downward from around chest height.

Now I'm sketching the trunk's curve as a sequence of points dropping down and curling slightly at the tip, and setting it up as a six-joint tentacle-type chain parented to the head. I want the radius to taper from a thick root to a thin tip, and I'm adding ridged ring wrinkles along its length using a paint function that cycles stripes based on position.

I'm also adding small finger-like lips at the trunk's end—an upper cone and lower lip shape—and deciding to keep the trunk hanging with a gentle forward S-curve rather than raised, with the tip resting just above the floor since only the feet should touch down. I'll build it low-poly with 8 sides and smooth skinning across the ring wrinkles.

For the mouth, I'm planning a separate jaw piece jointed near the trunk base, angled forward, with a small lower jaw box positioned under the trunk and an upper lip region above it, keeping the ring wrinkles as painted shading rather than actual geometry to save on complexity.

Now I'm plotting the tusks as curved ivory sprouts emerging from the upper jaw, following a path that dips forward-down before sweeping up and forward like real African elephant tusks, tapering from a thicker cream-colored base to a thin pointed tip.

I'm shading them with a gradient from tan-brown at the base to pale ivory toward the tip, with a dark gum ring marking the socket line. For the ears, I'm shaping large Africa-silhouette outlines sized about 1.1m wide and 1.4m tall, extruded and positioned on each side of the head with an outward tilt to match the sideways-facing ear plane.

Still working out ear orientation vectors...

Now I'm sketching the ear's outline shape in meters, plotting points from the root attachment up through a broad top curving down to a pointed lobe at the bottom, giving it that distinctive broad-top, tapered-bottom silhouette.

Sizing it against real African bush elephant proportions -- roughly 1.2m across and 1.65m tall seems right given how enormous their ears actually are. For the surface detail, I'm thinking through how to paint a pinkish-gray inner face with a darker mottled rim, possibly adding vein-like texture, though getting a true distance-to-edge gradient is tricky without a proper decal approach.

Still writing paint shader logic...

For the ear joint, I'm thinking through a hinge setup positioned near the ear base, aimed to let it flap outward, with the rest pose flared at roughly 25 degrees baked into the extrude direction rather than through posing.

For the head, I'm planning small dark eyes with amber rings on the sides, lashes, forehead domes for the parietal bumps, temple gland marks, and cheek wrinkle details, while considering a more faceted loft-based construction with octagonal cross-sections for a low-poly look.

Settling on ngon settings for the loft shapes — using an ngon value of 10 for the body and 8 for the legs to get faceted panels rather than smooth shading, and noting that the ngon approach adds a ridge vertex that could double as a spine ridge along the back. I'm also checking that elliptical width/height dimensions still work fine when paired with the ngon setting, then moving on to thinking about a limited color palette.

Now I'm picking out the full skin palette — warm gray-browns for the main coat, darker and lighter variants, pinkish ear tones, pale toenails, cream and brown tusk colors, dark eyes with an orange ring, plus ochre tones for dusty mud caked on the lower body. I'm planning to build the coat using a mottled paint pattern mixing two close grays, with wrinkle detailing layered on top.

Still working out the texture blending...

I'm calculating texel density for the paint atlas—checking whether 2048 or 4096 resolution gives crack patterns enough readable detail across the ~70 m² surface, leaning toward 2048 as a reasonable middle ground. Each leg sweep shares the same continuous paint definition as the body.

Now I'm thinking about adding skin wrinkle geometry beyond paint: small darker loop-sweeps around joints like ankles, knees, elbows, and neck to simulate skin folds, using thin torus-like rings cut across the bone at specific heights with a vertical direction vector, keeping the count low for a stylized low-poly look.

I also need toenails -- African elephants typically have 4 front toenails and 3 hind, so I'm placing small cream-colored wedge shapes around the front arc of each foot near the bottom edge, computing their positions around the foot's radius.

For the feet themselves, I'm adding a wider, flatter sole pad -- a short cylinder collar below the leg's taper, colored darker gray-cream to contrast with the body.

Next I'm building the tail: a chain of joints hanging from the rump down to around hip height, tapering in radius, with a coarse black spiky tuft at the tip made from a ring of small cone-like spikes. I'm also planning body details like a spine ridge and pelvis bone bumps for extra anatomical texture.

For mass, I'm adding scaled ellipsoid bumps at the hips and thighs to give volume to the bone structure, plus wider sweep radii at the top of the legs for thigh bulk. I'm also scattering sparse bristle hairs -- forehead tufts, chin hairs, and scattered strands on the back and head using simple thin-line hair cards.

I'm sketching the cheek and jaw details, a dark streaked temporal gland near the eye, and dome-shaped crown spheres for the forehead skull structure.

Now I'm working out the head loft geometry on the head bone, overlapping it with the body's neck connection so the silhouette reads as continuous, keeping the skin paint consistent to hide the seams.

Continuing the remaining loft stations down toward the face and trunk root, keeping proportions narrowing toward the front. I'm thinking through the real elephant head shape — steep forehead sloping down to the trunk base, face narrowing — to match the profile with an 8-gon cross-section.

I should add a separate lower jaw piece positioned below the head loft, then raise the head loft's bottom edge near the jaw so the jaw remains visible rather than being covered by the head geometry — adjusting stations 3 and 4's heights accordingly.

Then I'm working out the trunk's path and radius, starting broad at the root near the head and tapering as it curves downward and forward.

I'll shift the jaw back to z 2.6 to avoid trunk overlap. Then I'm working out the tusk paths with curving control points from base to tip, checking the segment lengths sum to roughly 2.1 units, consistent with realistic bush elephant tusk proportions.

Trimming the tusks slightly to 1.8m so the tip lands around z 4.3, keeping clear of the trunk's radius at that height, and confirming the overall model length from rump to tusk tip comes out to a believable 6.6m. I'm also adding a small base sheath ring in a tan gum color where the tusk meets the jaw, then moving on to positioning the eyes.

For the eyes, I'm computing their placement on the head loft surface near z 2.25, y 2.55, roughly ±0.4 on x given the head's narrowing width there, using a surface hit calculation to snap them onto the outer contour. Each eye gets a dark sphere for the pupil plus a flattened, darker socket shape and a wrinkled brow ridge swept above it to suggest age and character.

Now I'm working out ear placement, rooting them at the side of the head behind the eyes around [±0.45, 3.0, 1.85], then defining an outline that hangs downward from that attachment point, extending back in x and dropping from about y=0.1 to y=-1.55 to create the elephant's characteristic large, drooping ear shape.

Checking the cross product confirms the ear plane tilts reasonably, so I'll go with x=[0.45,0,-1] and y=[-0.1,1,0] since they're nearly orthogonal. The ear itself is two layers—a base slab plus a thicker rim—and I'll add a small joint at the attachment point for the ear bone.

I'm setting up a two-joint hinge chain for the ear so it can flex, tapering the thickness from thick near the head to thin at the lobe.

For remaining body details I'm deciding what to add versus skip: lighter belly paint, tail, knee wrinkle rings, toenails, and mud splash dust dots, while skipping things like navel or fold wrinkles. I'm also placing shoulder bulge spheres near the shoulder joints, scaled and positioned to blend with the skin tone and bound to the nearest bone.

Now I'm sketching the overall joint hierarchy, totaling roughly 45 joints across hips, spine, neck, head, jaw, trunk, four legs, tail, and ears. I'm starting to lay out the skeleton itself, beginning with the hips joint and its orientation, then building the spine chain as a smooth curve through several key points along the back.

I'm settling on a short two-span neck chain running up to the head joint, with the head parented off the neck's tip bone. For the body loft I'm mixing chains and joints together—spine, hips, and neck—spanning the z-range, then moving on to figure out how the front leg root joints should parent off the spine.

For the spine, I'm placing three joints along z (-1, 0, 1.0) and parenting the front shoulders off the topmost spine joint near z≈0.85, while the hind legs parent off the hips instead. For the leg chain itself, I'm working out the naming so four points map to three named spans plus an implicit tip, giving me shoulder, elbow, wrist, and foot joints for the front limb.

I'm tuning the segment lengths so the leg doesn't stretch into an unnaturally straight vertical column -- shortening the total reach to around 1.95 units split across upper, forearm, and cannon segments so a slight natural bend shows through when the inverse kinematics solves the pose.

For the hind leg, I'm setting the root height and segment lengths (0.9, 0.75, 0.45) to total slightly more than the target distance, with knee bending forward and hock bending back to get the characteristic hind-leg bend.

Now I'm working out the radius taper along the leg's profile, tapering down from a thicker root to a slimmer ankle before flaring slightly at the foot, using an 8-sided polygon cross-section with flat end caps for the sweep geometry.

For the foot itself, I'm building a flattened cylinder pad (wider at bottom, narrower at top) positioned so its bottom sits at ground level, matching where the leg sweep terminates, and considering adding a thicker fetlock cuff ring plus extending the pad slightly forward for a more elephant-like stance.

Now I'm routing the tail as a tapered sweep with a path curving back and down from the body's rear surface, checking it clears the hind leg thigh without overlap, and planning a dark spiky tuft at the tip.

For the head, I'm reconsidering the twin forehead domes typical of Asian elephants versus the rounder crown of African elephants—deciding to skip distinct domes and instead keep a single smoother crown shape, possibly with a subtle hair tuft on top, then moving on to shape cheek bulges.

Now I'm working on the lower jaw, mouth line, and pale jaw coloring, keeping details minimal, before focusing on the trunk tip—adding two small "finger" projections at the end and placing tiny dark nostril discs facing forward-down to suggest nostril openings.

Refining the trunk's final path with an S-curve so it tapers from the base down to a tip around z 3.5, with the tip's end cap facing forward-down to match the nostril placement.

For the surface texture, I'm working out periodic ring wrinkles along the trunk's arc length, darker grooves cycling roughly every 7-8cm, plus a lighter underside strip for the belly skin with its own crack pattern, blended via a paint function keyed on position along the path.

For the actual geometry, I'm deciding to keep an octagonal trunk cross-section and fake the rings purely through shading rather than extra geometry, since adding real radius wrinkles would multiply the triangle count unnecessarily -- though I note a cheap option using a triangular wave to perturb the radius slightly (~7%) with about 24 periods if I want physical ridges, estimating only ~450 extra triangles, well within budget.

I'm now roughing out a full parts budget across the model: legs, feet, nails, fold loops, trunk, fingers, head components, lashes, ears, tusks, gums, tail, bristles, and surface bumps, landing around 130-200 parts total, which feels reasonable for a detailed character rather than a simple diorama asset.

Beyond the base geometry I'm listing extra surface details to layer in -- cracked-skin texture, dust gradients, ear veins, toenails, tusk wear stains and chips, eyelashes, trunk rings, a tail tuft, fold creases near the neck and ears, and shoulder/hip bumps. I'm weighing whether to build the ear rim as a swept profile along the outline versus just extruding a slightly larger duplicate underneath to fake a rim-paint effect, leaning toward the simpler duplicate-extrude approach.

For the tusks, I'm planning a swept shape along a smooth curve with a tapered round-to-point cap, using a faceted hexagonal cross-section and a nested two-step color gradient fading from a brownish base stain near the root into ivory toward the tip, while skipping fine ring grooves and surface cracks for now to keep things simple.

Next I'm thinking through overall sizing — shoulder height around 3.2 units, head top near 3.3+, and overall height including ears around 3.35 — then shifting focus to placing the eyes on the loft surface, planning to rely on the preview/box check to verify positioning rather than computing exact surface widths by hand.

Still building the eye geometry...

Setting up the color palette now — skin tones, crack grooves, dust, ivory, tusks, eyes, hair, and mouth colors — plus a cracked-surface patch effect for texture and a dust gradient paint for the legs and lower body.

Defining ear inner/outer face thresholds, then working out vein geometry radiating from the ear root using angle and noise-based wobble to create a branching pattern...

Still refining ear material details... I'm also planning the outer skin face with a crack texture and darker rim, noting the paint function signature needs an unused parameter prefixed with underscore, and sketching a simple SVG hair strand for bristles using a curved path stroke.

For scatter patterns, I'm setting up bristle cards on the head crown using a surface scatter with randomized sizing and lean, filtered to areas with upward-facing normals near the top of the head, then adding sparser back hairs across the body where surfaces face upward, while deciding to skip chin hairs and instead focus on a tail tuft made from a ring of spikes.

Now I'm adding a second ring of tilted spikes to the tail, then moving on to skin creases around the leg joints—placing fold loops at specific heights along the front and hind legs to mark wrist, knee, and ankle regions, sweeping each loop with a thin radius and a dark groove color to make them read as recessed creases rather than raised ridges.

Adding toenail details to the feet...

Still defining nail geometry...

For the foot, I'll use a tapered cylinder with 8 sides positioned at the ankle joint, keeping the skin-tone paint consistent with the leg. The foot shape looks acceptable as is, so now I'm thinking through how the leg should taper and sweep to flat ends.

Checking leg placement relative to body width—front legs at x=0.55 and hind legs at x=0.6 might make the thighs bulge slightly beyond the torso, which actually reads nicely as shoulder muscle, so I'll keep that. The thigh and body overlap looks fine, and a slight forward lean on the front legs works for the pose. I'm ready to write the code now that proportions check out.

Now I'm working out the tail spikes—chaining the tail into named segments and placing rings of small spikes along it, tilted outward and downward to follow the tail's curve, with varying counts and radii at different points along its length.

I'm also adding a dark tuft capsule at the tail's end, then moving to the jaw: positioning a hinge joint, building a frustum box for the jaw shape sized to close neatly against the head without gaps, and considering a slightly lighter skin tone for the jaw's color.

Still placing facial details...

Now I'm defining the body loft station list with positions, widths, and heights along the torso to shape the overall silhouette.

The path's z-end segment belongs to the neck chain, so that lines up fine, and I'm okay with the belly sagging naturally at its lowest point. I'm placing the hips root centered in the body with the rear leg parented to it, and deciding to use a 10-sided ngon cross-section for the loft rather than a smooth circle. For the skin shading, I'm setting up a gradient keyed to absolute height, darker toward the belly and fading upward.

I'm tuning that gradient range and considering adding mottled dust patches as an overlay for extra texture, then moving on to importing the IK and math helpers and writing the base radius interpolation for the trunk shape.

Still refining trunk ridge pattern...

For the upper finger, I'm figuring out the tangent direction from the trunk's end point to orient a short spike cone, placing its base slightly offset upward from the tip with a small radius for a natural finger shape.

For the trunk tip, I'm adding two dark nostril discs as small flattened cylinders positioned symmetrically below center, and switching the sweep's end cap to flat so the finger and lip details cover the join cleanly instead of a rounded cap poking through.

I'm also planning the eye frame loop for left/right sides, and preparing to write the chain function with proper point arrays and typed parameters before testing it.

For the ear hinge joint, I'm working out the right axis orientation so the ear flaps naturally about its attachment point rather than an arbitrary direction, settling on aiming the joint roughly downward along the leading edge so the hinge rotation reads as a vertical flapping motion.

Now I'm plotting the ear's outline shape as a sequence of coordinate points going around the contour, building up the curve from the attachment point out to a sharp tip and back.

Checking clearance at z=0.85 and z=1.5 - the ear flares just enough to stay clear of the body width, with marginal overlap near the front that's fine since it'll be partially hidden. I'll set ear thickness tapering from 0.015 to 0.06 with a small bevel, then mirror the same ear geometry onto the s=-1 side, keeping the outline identical while flipping the normal direction.

For chains and joints I'll use the appropriate joint return types, and place the eye after the head loft is built. Building order should be skeleton first, then body, then head. Part count checks out, so I'm ready to write the full file.

input.command: mkdir -p scratch/africanElephantSonnet && ls samples | head -3; ls src
